Definition: from the same as G3008; functional publicly ("liturgic"); i.e. beneficient:--ministering.
BiblicalUsage: leitourgikós means ministering, and its few appearances are all worth reading. In Hebrews 1:14, "sent forth to minister for them who shall be heirs of salvation?".
TheologicalSignificance: I believe angels are ministering spirits sent to serve the heirs of salvation — unseen, unfailing, and on God's errand for me.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
